QuestionStmt.S: If a random variable $X$ follows the Binomial distribution $B(10, p)$ such that $5P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$, then the value of $\frac{P(X=5)}{P(X=6)}$ is equal to

Solution.S:
Given: $5P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$

For binomial distribution, $P(X = r) = {}^nC_r p^r q^{n-r}$.

Here $n = 10$.

$$5 \cdot {}^{10}C_0 (p)^0 q^{10} = {}^{10}C_1 p^1 q^9$$

$$5q^{10} = 10p q^9$$

$$5q = 10p \Rightarrow q = 2p$$

Since $p + q = 1$, we get $p + 2p = 1 \Rightarrow p = \frac{1}{3}$, $q = \frac{2}{3}$.

Now,

$$\frac{P(X=5)}{P(X=6)} = \frac{{}^{10}C_5 p^5 q^5}{{}^{10}C_6 p^6 q^4} = \frac{{}^{10}C_5}{{}^{10}C_6} \cdot \frac{q}{p}$$

$$= \frac{252}{210} \cdot \frac{2/3}{1/3} = \frac{6}{5} \cdot 2 = \frac{12}{5}$$

Hence, the correct option is C.
